why: Quote is verbatim (first sentence of plugin-hints.md line 17) and the cited file:line is exactly as claimed (apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:60-62 destructures CLAUDECODE out of the child env with the stated Claude-SDK-nesting reason; packages/server/src/__tests__/smoke.test.ts:44,173 do the same). The finding fails on the other two checks. (1) DELIBERATE PRODUCT DIFFERENCE. Read whole, this page defines one mechanism: CLAUDECODE (and CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION from v2.1.172) gates a CLI's <claude-code-hint /> stderr marker, and line 149 states 'The hint protocol only takes effect for plugins listed in the official Anthropic marketplace, claude-plugins-official. Anthropic curates that marketplace at its discretion' — a rebranded T-Bank fork cannot list there, so the protocol has no terminus for us. Asserting CLAUDECODE=1 from a non-Claude product is a brand claim, and it contradicts a boundary this repo records in shipped source: packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:94-96 — the generic plugin runtime env 'Emits Nessy names plus the unbranded PLUGIN_* compatibility aliases — never Claude aliases' — with CLAUDE_* names emitted ONLY under an explicit per-plugin claude-plugin-env-v1 / codex-plugin-env-v1 compat profile (data-paths.ts:111-155). A blanket CLAUDECODE=1 on every Bash and hook subprocess has no such profile. (2) THE CLAIMED OUR-STATE IS FALSE AS AN ABSOLUTE. Bash-tool subprocesses do not get the raw host env: local-tools/runtime.ts:232-259 routes through runCommand into ProcessSupervisor, which defaults to the 'restricted' environment profile (process-supervisor.ts:717-733) whose hostEnvironment() filters process.env through the RESTRICTED_HOST_ENVIRONMENT allowlist at process-supervisor.ts:703-711. That allowlist contains NESSY_AGENT_VERSION, which apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:145 sets to app.getVersion() in the same process that constructs SessionManager (index.ts:711) and therefore the supervisor (SessionManager.ts:3574). So in the packaged desktop app every Bash-tool subprocess DOES carry a Nessy-presence env marker; what is missing is only that it wears a name third-party CLIs do not know. Separately, on the Claude backend (NESSY_FEATURE_PROVIDER_CLAUDE=1) the vendored node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk-darwin-arm64/claude binary — 19 CLAUDECODE occurrences — is what runs Bash, so those subprocesses get the real marker from Claude Code itself; that is precisely why server-spawner.ts:62 must strip it. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS INVERTED. There is no <claude-code-hint /> reader anywhere in packages/ or apps/ (grep -ra, zero hits outside docs). Setting CLAUDECODE=1 would make gating CLIs emit raw hint tags that Nessy cannot strip, injecting them into model context — a regression, not a fix. The two absences are coupled and coherent, and the restricted allowlist already strips an inherited CLAUDECODE from Bash subprocesses, so the phase1 companion worry ('any CLI that gates on a variable we do inherit would leak the raw tag') is handled one layer down as well. Not listed in inert-worklist section 3 or 4, but it is the product-difference carve-out the task names.
correctedState: Nessy does not set CLAUDECODE, and deliberately so: the variable's only documented role on this page is gating a <claude-code-hint /> marker whose install prompt fires only for Anthropic's curated claude-plugins-official marketplace, which this fork cannot use, and the repo records the rule that Claude-branded env names are emitted only under an explicit per-plugin compat profile (packages/shared/src/plugins/data-paths.ts:94-96, :141-155), which a blanket Bash/hook variable has none. It is also not true that no marker reaches tool subprocesses: those run under the 'restricted' environment profile whose allowlist (process-supervisor.ts:703-711) admits NESSY_AGENT_VERSION, set by apps/electron/src/main/index.ts:145 in the same process as the supervisor, so packaged-app Bash subprocesses carry a Nessy-presence marker under a Nessy name; that same allowlist strips any inherited CLAUDECODE. On the opt-in Claude backend the bundled claude-agent-sdk binary sets CLAUDECODE itself, which is why apps/cli/src/server-spawner.ts:62 removes it to clear the SDK's nesting guard. The only real residue is that third-party CLIs cannot recognise the Nessy-named marker — and since Nessy has no reader for the hint tag, adopting the Claude name would leak raw <claude-code-hint /> lines into model context rather than gain anything.
